In Serbia, a group of candidates selected by students is posing a major challenge to
the government in parliamentary elections.
This follows two years of protests accusing the country's long-serving populist leader,
Alexander Vucic, of corruption.
Guy Delornay reports from Belgrade.
There are no students on the student list political ticket.
Instead, young people at Serbia's universities have selected 250 candidates they say are
experts in their fields.
Together, they'll form the main opposition against Serbia's populist leader, Alexander
Vucic.

Vucic insists he's the only man who can take the country forward.

Now the voters must decide who they believe.
For NPR News, I'm Guy Delornay in Belgrade, Serbia.
